entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q1
entry.itemBody: When preparing the cash-flow forecasts for both projects, Soroka should include:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. Capital allocation analysis should include only incremental cash flows associated with a new investment. The loss of revenue from existing products is an incremental negative effect that should be included in the analysis. The market research costs in this case are a sunk cost because the research has already been completed and therefore does not affect cash -flow estimates, no matter whether ABC undertakes either of these projects or neither of them.

choices.itemBody: A. only the cost of the market research.
B. only the loss of revenue from existing products.
C. both the market research cost and the loss of revenue from existing products.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q2
entry.itemBody: With regard to Project A and Project B, which of the following is true?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The IRR decision rule is to invest if the IRR exceeds the required rate of return or hurdle rate. Project B’s IRR is 8.97%, which exceeds the required rate of return of 8%; however, Project A’s IRR is 7.04%, which is below the required rate of return of 8%. The NPV of both projects can be calculated as follows: 𝑁𝑃𝑉𝐴 = −18.5 + 4.5 (1 + 0.08)1 + 6 (1 + 0.08)2 + 6 (1 + 0.08)3 + 5.5 (1 + 0.08)4 = −0.38 𝑁𝑃𝑉𝐵 = −33.5 + −2.5 (1 + 0.08)1 + −2.5 (1 + 0.08)2 + 24 (1 + 0.08)3 + 25.5 (1 + 0.08)4 = 1.12 Using the same equation, we can solve for the IRRs by assuming that NPV = 0. 0 = −18.5 + 4.5 (1 + IRR𝐴)1 + 6 (1 + IRR𝐴)2 + 6 (1 + IRR𝐴)3 + 5.5 (1 + IRR𝐴)4 IRR𝐴 = 7.04% 0 = −33.5 + −2.5 (1 + IRR𝐵)1 + −2.5 (1 + IRR𝐵)2 + 24 (1 + IRR𝐵)3 + 25.5 (1 + IRR𝐵)4 IRR𝐵 = 8.97%

choices.itemBody: A. Both projects should be invested in according to the IRR decision rule.
B. Both projects should be invested in according to the NPV decision rule.
C. Only Project B should be invested in according to the IRR decision rule.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q3
entry.itemBody: The most likely impact from the cash -flow timing considered by Soroka is that:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. The forecasted timing of cash flow is an important factor affecting both projects’ IRR and NPV. In the case of delaying all future cash flows from both projects by six months, the result would be a lower IRR and a lower NPV. Given that all future cash flows are to be received six months later, their present value decreases; hence, the NPV and IRR of an entire project also decrease. B is incorrect because when cash flows from the investment projects are delayed by six months, both projects’ NPV and IRR would decrease, not stay unchanged. C is incorrect because when cash flows from the investment projects are delayed by six months, both project’s NPV and IRR would decrease.

choices.itemBody: A. both IRR and NPV would decrease.
B. both IRR and NPV stay unchanged.
C. only IRR would decrease but NPV would increase.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q5
entry.itemBody: Considering ABC management’s ROIC-based investment criterion and the IRR and NPV of both projects, Soroka should recommend to:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. ABC’s management aims to achieve a minimum ROIC above 9.20%, but the IRR of both projects fails to meet this investment criterion. Even though Project B has a positive NPV, if it were undertaken, it would reduce ROIC. B is incorrect because even though Project B’s NPV is $1.12 million (which increases ABC’s value to shareholders), its IRR is 8.97%, which is below the target ROIC of 9.20%. Consequently, if Project B was undertaken, it would lower ABC’s ROIC. C is incorrect because Project A’s I RR is below ABC management’s target ROIC of 9.2%. Additionally, Project A’s NPV is negative, so it decreases ABC’s shareholder value.

choices.itemBody: A. reject both projects A and B.
B. invest only in Project B because it has a higher NPV.
C. invest only in Project A because has positive cash flow during all four years.

entry.itemBody: The incremental after-tax cash flows (in € thousands) and information on two mutually exclusive projects are as follows: Year 0 1 2 3 4 Net Present Value (NPV, € thousands) Internal Rate of Return (IRR, %) Project X −15,000 2,000 5,000 8,000 8,000 354 16 Project Y −13,250 200 500 7,000 15,000 --- --- The appropriate hurdle rate to use in evaluating the projects is 15.0%. Which of the following statements is most accurate? The company should accept:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. entry.itemBody: A project has the following annual cash flows: Year 0 Year 1 Year 2 Year 3 Year 4 ‒$4,662,005 $22,610,723 ‒$41,072,261 $33,116,550 ‒$10,000,000 Which of the following discount rates most likely produces the highest net present value (NPV)?

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q9
entry.itemBody: A measure of how effectively capital is converted into after-tax operating profits is the:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because ROIC reflects how effectively a company’s management is able to convert capital into after-tax operating profits.

choices.itemBody: C. return on invested capital. Capital Investments and Capital Allocation Faculty: Page 4 of 12

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q10
entry.itemBody: Which of the following is considered a capital allocation pitfall? Basing investment decisions on:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because one common pitfall is basing investment decisions on EPS, net income, or ROE: Companies sometimes have incentives to boost earnings per share, net income, or return on equity. Many investments, even those with strong NPVs, do not increase these accounting numbers in the short run and may even reduce them. entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q11
entry.itemBody: When choosing between mutually exclusive projects, an analyst should:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because when the choice is between two mutually exclusive projects and the NPV and IRR rank the two projects differently, the NPV criterion is strongly preferred. We referred to the rate used in discounting the cash flows as the “required rate of return.” The required rate of return is the discount rate that the issuer’s suppliers of capital require given the riskiness of the project. This discount rate is frequently called the “opportunity cost of funds” or the “cost of capital.” For a capital investment with one investment outlay, made initially, the net present value (NPV) is the present value of the future after -tax cash flows minus the investment outlay, where the discount rate equals the required rate of return.

choices.itemBody: A. accept the project with the highest IRR.
B. use the opportunity cost of funds as the discount rate.
C. accept the projects for which the IRR is greater than the opportunity cost of funds.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q12
entry.itemBody: A company is evaluating the following mutually exclusive capital projects: Project 1 Project 2 NPV $180,000 $100,000 IRR 10% 15% If the hurdle rate is 8%, the company should invest in:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because Project 1 has a higher NPV. For mutually exclusive investments that are ranked differently by the NPV and IRR, the NPV criterion is more economically sound.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q13
entry.itemBody: Compared to going concern projects, expansion projects most likely involve:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because expansion projects typically involve greater uncertainty, time, and amounts of capital than going concern projects.

choices.itemBody: C. both greater uncertainty and greater amounts of capital.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q14
entry.itemBody: An electric vehicle manufacturer invests in a new technology to meet new safety standards. This project is best classified as a(n):

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because regulatory and compliance projects are required by third parties, such as government regulatory bodies, to meet safety and regulatory compliance standards. The investment in new technology to meet improved safety standards is therefore a compliance project.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q15
entry.itemBody: A company should exercise the abandonment option on an investment if the present value of the cash flows from continuing the investment is:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because if the cash flow from abandoning an investment exceeds the present value of the cash flows from continuing the investment, the company should exercise the abandonment option. Conversely, if the PV of the cash flows from continuing the investment is lower than the cash flow from abandoning the investment, the company should exercise the abandonment option.

choices.itemBody: A. lower than the cash flow from abandoning the investment.
B. the same as the cash flow from abandoning the investment.
C. greater than the cash flow from abandoning the investment.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q16
entry.itemBody: A company with a required rate of return of 12% is considering a capital project with the following cash flows (in millions): Initial Outlay Year 1 Year 2 Cash flow −£150 £8 £175 Capital Investments and Capital Allocation Faculty: Page 5 of 12 The expected IRR for this project is most likely:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the IRR is the discount rate that makes the present value of the future after-tax cash flows equal that investment outlay or ∑nt=1 CFt ÷ (1 + IRR)t = Outlay, where IRR is the internal rate of return. Solved using the following calculator inputs: CF0 = −150, CF1 = 8, CF2 = 175, Calculate IRR = 10.7119, rounded to 10.71% which is less than 12%.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q17
entry.itemBody: Subsequent to making a capital investment, a company reacts to poor financial results from the project by abandoning it. This action alone best exemplifies the exercise of a:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because sizing options encompass abandonment or expansion of capacity. If after investing the company can abandon the investment if the financial results are disappointing, it has an abandonment option. At some future date, if the cash flow from abandoning an investment exceeds the present value of the cash flows from continuing the investment, the company should exercise the abandonment option. Conversely, if the company can make additional investments when future financial results are strong, the company has a growth option or an expansion option. Capital Investments and Capital Allocation Faculty: Page 11 of 12

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q18
entry.itemBody: An analyst gathers the following information about a project: Initial outlay €100 million Cash flow at end of Year 1 €65 million Cash flow at end of Year 2 €65 million Cash flow at end of Year 3 €65 million If the required rate of return is 15%, the NPV is closest to:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because it discounts all the cash flows at the required return and sums them as follows: NPV = t=1nΣCFt /(1 + r)t − Outlay, where CFt = After-tax cash flow at time t, r = Required rate of return for the investment, Outlay = Investment cash flow at time zero, NPV = 65/(1 + 15%) + 65/(1 + 15%)2 + 65/(1 + 15%)3 – 100 ≈ 56.52 + 49.15 + 42.74 – 100 = 148.41 ≈ 48.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q19
entry.itemBody: The NPV of a new project is expected to be –$0.20 million. An incremental investment of $0.40 million would give management the flexibility to switch to a lower cost input in the future. If this option has an estimated value of $0.80 million, the value of the project including the option is:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the NPV, including the real option, should be: Project NPV = NPV (based on DCF alone) – Cost of options + Value of options. Project NPV = –$0.2 million – $0.4 million + $0.8 million = $0.2 million.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q20
entry.itemBody: A company is deciding whether to invest in one of two mutually exclusive projects with positive NPVs. If Project 1 has a higher NPV but a lower IRR than Project 2, the company should:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because when the choice is between two mutually exclusive projects and the NPV and IRR rank the two projects differently, the NPV criterion is strongly preferred. ... As a practical matter, once a corporation has the data to calculate the NPV, it is fairly trivial to then calculate the IRR and other capital allocation criteria. However, the most appropriate and theoretically sound criterion is the NPV.

choices.itemBody: C. be indifferent between Project 1 and Project 2.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q21
entry.itemBody: Management most likely has the least amount of discretion when deciding to invest in a(n):

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because unlike going concern and expansion projects, for which management has discretion in deciding whether or not to invest, regulatory and compliance projects are required by third parties, such as government regulatory bodies, to meet safety and regulatory compliance standards.

choices.itemBody: C. going concern project. Capital Investments and Capital Allocation Faculty: Page 6 of 12

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q22
entry.itemBody: The ability to abandon an investment if it has produced disappointing financial results is most likely a type of:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because an abandonment option is a type of sizing option. If after investing the company can abandon the investment if the financial results are disappointing, it has an abandonment option. At some future date, if the cash flow from abandoning an investme nt exceeds the present value of the cash flows from continuing the investment, the company should exercise the abandonment option.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q23
entry.itemBody: Which statement regarding capital investments is correct?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because capital investments are also usually necessary if an established firm decides to extend its existing operations to adjacent products and services or expand to new regions or markets.

choices.itemBody: A. Going concern projects are investments to increase the size of the business
B. Regulatory compliance projects seldom increase a firm’s expenses with no added revenue
C. Capital investments are usually necessary if a firm extends its existing operations to adjacent products and services

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q24
entry.itemBody: Maintenance capital expenditures include:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because continuous improvements of existing facilities are going concern projects. Going concern projects, often known as maintenance capital expenditures, are investments to continue the company’s current operations and maintain the existing size of the business. Common going concern projects include replacing assets nearing the end of their useful life, maintaining IT hardware and software, and continuous improvements of existing facilities.

choices.itemBody: C. investing in solar panel production to benefit from government subsidies.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q25
entry.itemBody: Which of the following is a common capital allocation pitfall?

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because this is often a sign of inertia, which is a common mistake in capital allocation. Inertia is the result of management anchoring their capital investment budgets to prior year amounts. If capital investment each year is static or increasing despite falling returns on investment, the analyst should question the issuer’s justification for its capital investment and whether management should be considering alternative uses. Capital Investments and Capital Allocation Faculty: Page 12 of 12

choices.itemBody: B. Anchoring capital investment budgets to prior year amounts
C. Considering different states of the world for investment alternatives

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q26
entry.itemBody: With respect to capital budgeting, which of the following statements is most accurate? The internal rate of return calculation assumes that a project's interim cash flows are reinvested at the project's:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because the IRR assumes reinvestment at the IRR. Mathematically, whenever you discount a cash flow at a particular discount rate, you are implicitly assuming that you can reinvest a cash flow at that same discount rate.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q27
entry.itemBody: When evaluating potential capital investments, the most appropriate discount rate is the:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because the required rate of return for an investment is the rate of return that a corporate issuer’s investors could earn on a similarly risky investment.

choices.itemBody: A. overall cost of capital for the company.
B. individual investment's required rate of return.
C. cost of debt or cost of equity, depending on the financing source.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q28
entry.itemBody: An analyst gathers the following information (in $ millions) about two mutually exclusive capital projects: NPV at 9% Required Rate of Return NPV at 12% Required Rate of Return NPV at 15% Required Rate of Return Project 1 50 17 −10 Project 2 61 13 −31 Capital Investments and Capital Allocation Faculty: Page 7 of 12 Project 1 should be selected for investment if the required rate of return is:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because the decision rule for the NPV is: Invest if NPV > 0. In the case of mutually exclusive investment projects, a company should choose the one with the higher NPV.

entry.title: 2027 Corporate Finance Mod5-Q30
entry.itemBody: A firm is considering a project that would require an initial investment of THB270 million (Thai baht). The project will help increase the firm’s after -tax net cash flows by THB30 million per year in perpetuity, and it is found to have a negative NPV of THB20 million. The IRR (%) of the project is closest to:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. The IRR is the discount rate that makes the NPV = 0. Because the cash flow stream is in perpetuity, it can be solved as follows: 0 = –270 + (30/IRR) IRR = 11.1%.
